nodes.label: Operator
nodes.blurb: The person who operates this system. The credential is a label inside systems you author — it is not proof of anything outside them.

nodes.label: CrystalCore.OS
nodes.blurb: Sovereign runtime and OS frame. The house the doors belong to.

nodes.label: Consent gate
nodes.blurb: Five doors, fail-closed: revocation, approval, provenance, permission, scope. The ask is recorded before any of them is opened.

nodes.label: Memory layers
nodes.blurb: episodic · semantic · reflective. Working memory — the live conversation — is never guest-readable and deliberately not grantable. The structure is the taxonomy; there is no per-entry type field.

nodes.label: CrystalBridge
nodes.blurb: Guest agency in tools — act, return. Today only the semantic layer is actually served, because it is the only layer with per-entry visibility consent.

nodes.label: Audit · pending · revoke
nodes.blurb: Inspectable consent history. Every decision is appended; every ask is recorded before it is answered; revocation survives restart.

doors.label: Revocation
doors.asks: Has the human withdrawn this guest's consent?
doors.detail: Read from the append-only ledger on every check, so a revocation bites without a restart and survives every restart. A ledger that cannot be read refuses everyone — a gate that cannot know who is revoked must not guess.
doors.refuses: guest '<name>' has been revoked by the human — reinstate with --reinstate before it can act again

doors.label: Approval
doors.asks: Is this guest approved at all?
doors.detail: Nothing is granted by default. Absence of a grant is absence of consent, not legacy access.

doors.label: Provenance
doors.asks: Does the presented token prove this is really the named guest?
doors.detail: Launcher authentication — possession of a per-guest minted secret — stated as exactly that, not cryptographic identity of a remote model. Origin that cannot be established is treated exactly like absent consent.
doors.refuses: provenance for guest '<name>' could not be established — token missing or wrong

doors.label: Permission
doors.asks: May it call this specific tool?
doors.detail: Per-tool, not per-guest-in-general. Reaching the door is not the same as being let through it.
doors.refuses: guest '<name>' has no permission for tool '<tool>'

doors.label: Scope
doors.asks: Which visibility classes, and which memory layers?
doors.detail: Two independent axes: visibility (private / shared) and memory type (episodic / semantic / reflective). A grant with no types refuses, and says what to add. Only the semantic layer is actually served today.
doors.refuses: tool '<tool>' serves the <layer> layer and guest '<name>' is granted only <types> — nothing behind this door for that grant

doors_note: Before any door is opened, the ask itself is written to pending.jsonl. An ask that cannot be recorded refuses rather than acting unobservably — that is the recorder failing, not consent deciding, which is why it is not a sixth door.

flow.label: Baseline
flow.detail: Check the baseline before acting. No Operator Card exists to hold this language — the step is drawn as designed, not built.

flow.label: One command
flow.detail: The operator surface that actually exists today: revoke, reinstate, mint a token, review memories. Each takes a reason, and each is mirrored into the audit log.

flow.label: Stand down
flow.detail: Close the terminal and let ordinary life outrank it. No implementation holds this step either — it is a shape, honestly labelled.
